annotationRationale: The solution combines case counting with successive choices, then divides successful sequences by equally likely outcomes. Cube edge structure and three-dimensional coordinates justify which moves are allowed.
sourceMethod: Followed the official successive-move count, with 6 first moves, 4 second moves, and two third-move cases contributing 2·2+1·3 completions. Coordinates clarify every allowed direction and why square paths are counted only once.

review.mathCheck: There are 24 permissible first-two-move sequences. Each has 2·2+3=7 completions, giving 168 successful sequences among 1296 equally likely outcomes. The probability is 7/54, choice B; square closures are counted once.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, originally worded adaptation of MAA Q24, p.14: perpendicular first moves, two spatial third-move choices with two completions each, and one square-shaped third-move choice with three completions.
review.annotationCheck: Coordinate spans, retraced edges, symmetry and the two cubes sharing a square are handled explicitly. The argument needs no additional figure and is suitable for AMC 10.
